About Us
Since 2014 Thornton Heath Nursery School has been successfully led and managed by Pegasus Academy Trust on behalf of the local authority, providing young children with the very best start to their educational journey.
A welcome from the Head of Nursery
It is with great pleasure that we welcome you to Thornton Heath Nursery School!
Set back from the main roads and tucked away from the hustle and bustle of the High Street, our nursery is a hidden gem. Inside, you’ll find surprisingly spacious and thoughtfully designed indoor areas, and outside, a breathtaking learning space that inspires imagination and a love of nature.
Thornton Heath Nursery School has built a strong reputation as a caring and inclusive setting, where children are nurtured, celebrated, and supported to thrive. Parents regularly express high levels of satisfaction with the warm welcome they receive and the positive progress their children make.
Our calm and engaging learning environments are ever-changing to spark curiosity and encourage exploration. We promote independence, resilience, and a “can do” attitude, helping our children to grow into confident learners. Kindness is at the heart of everything we do – we support children to build positive relationships using kind words, kind hands, and collaborative play.
All staff are committed to our culture of safeguarding. They are highly skilled and experienced in working with young children and their families, and make children’s safety and wellbeing a top priority in all aspects of nursery life.
We’re especially proud of our welcoming community, inclusive ethos, and strong track record of supporting children with additional needs. Most importantly, we are proud of our joyful, confident and resilient children, who leave us ready for the next stage of their learning journey.
We hope this website gives you a glimpse of what makes our school so special – and we warmly invite you to come and experience it for yourself.
Jenette IndarsinghHead of Nursery

Breakfast, lunch and after school care
Early birds (Breakfast club)
Care at the beginning of the day is provided in the Sunshine Room – a dedicated space with its own kitchen. By ringing on the main school buzzer after 8:00am parents can be seen on CCTV and staff will come and let you in as the usual reception area is not generally open at this time. Care is provided between 8:00am and 8:30am at a cost of £4 per day – which includes breakfast.
In order to be as flexible as possible we allow parents to use this service on a ‘pay as you go’ basis – i.e. you do not have to pay for a whole week at a time. If you wish your child to use this service you should register in the nursery office.
The cost is £4.00 per day and the club does not accept payments in cash. Parents must pay by our ‘Magic Booking’ facility.
Early morning extended hour for full-time children
For parents that are entitled to 30 hour funded places, there is an option to purchase an additional hour at the beginning of our school day from 08.30am – 09.30am at a cost of £40 per week giving your child an extra five hours of learning per week. An 08.30am start also supports school readiness preparation and gives you an opportunity to embed those early morning routines before moving on to primary school. Many parents have commented that it also provides them with additional time for their onward journey after dropping their child to the nursery.
This must be booked and paid for through ‘Magic Booking’, the nursery does not accept payments in cash.
Sunshine Club (After school club)
Our after school club is known as the “Sunshine Club” and offers parents the facility to balance busy schedules whilst being safe in the knowledge that their child/children are having fun and being well cared for at the end of the nursery school day.
Sunshine Club is run “in house” by members of the THNS staff team and it is only available to children who attend Thornton Heath Nursery School.
Held in our Sunshine Room, our Sunshine Club provides an inviting environment where children can continue their learning through play or relax after a busy day! The Sunshine Room is fully equipped with its own kitchen for preparing a snack or “light” tea as well as having its own outdoor learning area.
From 15.30 – 16.00 £5 daily
From 15.30 – 17.00 £10 daily
From 15.30 – 18.00 £15 daily
A fine of £1 per minute will be charged if your child is collected later than their booked time.
Parents can book on a ‘ad hoc’ basis although bookings must be made by 12 midday on the day you wish to use the service. We can not accept any bookings after 12 midday, this is to ensure we adhere to safety guidelines. All bookings must be made through Magic Booking. You will not be able to contact the school office and book your child in on a daily basis, we need to know in advance how many children will be attending so that we can prepare the provision.
For more information about this service and how to book please contact the school office on 020 86840494 or click here.
We look forward to welcoming your child to the Sunshine Club.

Governors
The main aim of the governing body of Thornton Heath Nursery School is to maintain and improve the standards of education.
Our work is divided into four key areas:
Staff Governors can include both teaching and non-teaching staff. Staff governors are elected by the staff and should communicate with those who elect them. Co-opted governors are appointed by the governing body. Co-opted governors are people who, in the opinion of the governing body, have skills required to contribute to the effective governance and success of the school. Local Authority Governors are nominated by the local authority but appointed by the governing body. The local authority can nominate any eligible person as a local authority governor, but it is for the governing body to decide whether the person meets their eligibility criteria. Parent Governors are elected to be representative of the parent body. If there are not enough nominations, the governing body can appoint parent governors. Parent governors may complete their term of office when their child leaves the school.

Full Governing Body Minutes

Jenette Indarsingh (Head of Nursery)
Lynne Sampson
I have been working in education since 1986 starting my career in the London Borough of Bexley. After teaching at two schools in three key stages I moved to Whitehorse Manor Infants becoming the deputy in 1992 and the head in 1997.
In 2007 the school was judged to be outstanding and following that I was asked by the DfE to become a Local Leader in Education and support schools in difficulty.
In 2010, along with Jolyon Roberts who was then the head at Whitehorse Manor Juniors, I asked to become an academy sponsor and together we set up The Pegasus Academy Trust. To date we have been successful in “turning round” Ecclesbourne Primary School, Beulah Infant and Nursery School and Thornton Heath Nursery which are now judged to be good schools with outstanding features. We have been working with Cypress Primary which has now been judged as a good school.
Cheridah Mejias
I am a registered Manager of The Little Flower Respite home and I have over 25 years experience of working with children within the care sector. In 2006 I completed my NVQ Level 3 in Health and Social Care and my NVQ Level 5 in care management in 2011. Doing both the NVQ Level 3 and Level 5 gave me an insight as to what is required to run a home. Over the last 25 years I have amassed valuable knowledge in relation in working with children. In February 2009 I started a contract with the London Borough of Croydon to provide respite care for high dependency physically disabled children and because of the positive experience of working with disabled children and their families, I decided to open up a small home in order to provide respite care to high dependency physically disabled children. I am looking forward to sharing my knowledge as part of the Governing Body of THNS in order to support the children and families in our local area.
Jenette Indarsingh
Head of Nursery, Designated Safeguarding Lead, SENDCO
I have been working in education since 1995, always working in Thornton Heath. After teaching at Beulah Infant School for a year, I became the maths leader for the school, working alongside the local education authority to promote outstanding practice in the teaching of maths across the borough. I then became the assessment leader at Beulah as well as a KS1 moderator for Croydon. In 2010 I became the Deputy Head at Beulah. I was instrumental in securing the best possible outcome for Beulah as they joined Pegasus Academy Trust in 2014 and in 2017 my leadership skills were judged to be outstanding by Ofsted. In May 2018 I gained my National Professional Qualification for Headship.
As the Head of Nursery, I am wholly committed to leading an outstanding provision for our local children and their families. I believe that THNS is a unique setting where we have high standards for our staff and children. We support every child at THNS to reach their full potential within a nurturing environment.

“Play is the highest expression of human development in childhood, for it alone is the free expression of what is in a child’s soul.”– Friedrich Froebel
Our Approach to Learning Through Play
At Thornton Heath Nursery School, we believe that play is the foundation of lifelong learning. Through a play-based approach, children become inquisitive, resilient, and enthusiastic learners, setting them up for success throughout their educational journey.
Play-based learning is central to everything we do. It supports children’s social and emotional development, builds their confidence and motivation, and strengthens vital skills like language, early maths, and problem-solving. Through play, children learn to take initiative, stay focused, and explore the world around them with curiosity and joy.
We combine rich, child-led play with carefully planned focused learning sessions to ensure every child receives a balanced and high-quality early education. This approach allows us to support each child holistically, helping them to grow not just academically, but emotionally and socially too.
We value and celebrate the uniqueness of every child. Each child arrives with their own interests, strengths, and personality. Our experienced staff observe closely and thoughtfully plan opportunities that build on what each child already knows and can do, moving their learning forward in meaningful ways.
We follow the Statutory Framework for the Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS), which sets the standards for learning, development and care for children from birth to age five. The EYFS outlines seven areas of learning, all equally important, and further broken down into specific aspects (listed below).

Through a well-balanced mix of child-led play and adult-guided experiences, we support children’s development across all these areas in a way that is meaningful, joyful, and suited to their individual needs.
How Children Learn: The Characteristics of Effective Teaching and Learning
At Thornton Heath Nursery School, we understand that how children learn is just as important as what they learn. The Characteristics of Effective Teaching and Learning, as outlined in the EYFS, help us support children in becoming confident, curious, and independent learners.
Every child learns in their own unique way, and these characteristics help us recognise and nurture positive learning behaviours:
These characteristics are like a “golden thread” running through all areas of learning. They shape the way children approach new experiences and help build the foundations for lifelong learning.
Planning for Play and Progress
Our skilled staff thoughtfully plan activities and experiences across all seven areas of learning, both indoors and outdoors. Planning is flexible and often guided by the children’s own interests, allowing learning to stay meaningful, exciting, and relevant. As children’s interests evolve, our plans do too.
While much of the learning is child-led through play, we also provide small group sessions each day—usually twice per session—often led by each child’s key person. These focused times support early skills in communication, literacy, maths, and more.
Our Curriculum Goals
We’ve carefully considered what we hope each child will achieve during their time with us. Our curriculum goals are designed to give children the key skills and confidence they need for the next step in their learning journey. Each goal links closely to the EYFS areas of learning and supports their all-round development.
You can see our curriculum goals displayed in the main entrance or explore them further here, where we also explain why each goal was chosen.

SEND Information
In 2021 1.4% of children in state-funded nurseries had an ‘Educational Health Care Plan’ – known as a ECHP. In addition to this 14.5% of children in state-funded nurseries received some sort of SEN support.
The most common type of need for those with SEN support is speech, language and communication needs.
What are special educational needs for young children?
Children who are under compulsory school age have a special educational need and/or disability (also known as SEND) if they have a learning difficulty or disability that is likely to require special educational provision when they reach compulsory school age. For children under the age of two, special educational provision means educational provision of any kind, including home-based programmes.
What are the requirements for early years providers?
The Early Years Foundation Stage (EYFS) Framework requires all early years providers to have arrangements in place to support children with SEN or disabilities and provide parents with information on this. It is a mandatory requirement that maintained nursery schools employ a qualified Special Educational Needs Co-ordinator (SENCO), at Thornton Heath Nursery School this is Jenette Indarsingh (Head of Nursery, QTS, PGCE SENCO).
The links below explain what Thornton Heath Nursery School and Croydon are able to offer families whose children have special educational needs and/or disabilities.
What is the Local Offer?
Local Authorities must publish a Local Offer which sets out in one place information about the available provision in their area across education, health and social care for children and young people with SEND, including those who do not have EHC plans. Croydon’s Local Offer can be found here.

Our friendly office staff will tell you what you need to bring with you for your admission appointment.
We look forward to receiving your application and welcoming you to our Thornton Heath Nursery School family.

Bubbles and Biters!
This week’s Rhyme Time was 1,2,3,4,5 (Once I Caught a Fish Alive!). The garden became a prime fishing ground with biting fish being hung on the line using hooks, pipe cleaners and pegs…all tricky fasteners enabling small hands and fingers to grow big muscles!
Kamile the scientist perfected her bubble formula, ready to teach the children how to make it next week…for this week the children were simply the bubble wand blowers…next week they shall be measuring, pouring and inventing their own bubble wands!

More Pizza Please!
From expertly plucking only the ripe tomatoes from our dense canopy of tomato plants, to harvesting the basil whilst carefully moving the resident shield bugs; the children of Thornton Heath Nursery School not only understand from where their food comes from, they have worked hard to grow it and have continued to care for it themselves. They are developing the muscle strength and coordination to combine, squash, knead and roll their own school grown produce…transforming it into their favourite snack time treat.
